title: Professional Mastery
subtitle: Command the boardroom: corporate rhetoric, high-stakes negotiation, and the voice of expert counsel

lessons.title: Le discours d'entreprise
lessons.description: The rhetoric of corporate speech: rallying a team, framing bad news, deploying corporate jargon, and knowing when to abandon it for the plain truth.

blocks.heading: Le discours mobilisateur : galvaniser sans mentir
blocks.body: Corporate rallying speech aims to unite a team behind a shared goal, but the C2-level distinction is doing so without slipping into empty cheerleading. A convincing speaker names the difficulty honestly, builds ambition through concrete stakes, and paints the vision with vivid imagery rather than numbers alone.

examples.french: Ce trimestre a été difficile ; le prochain sera décisif.
examples.english: This quarter was difficult; the next will be decisive.

examples.french: Je ne vous demande pas d'y croire aveuglément, mais de le construire avec moi.
examples.english: I'm not asking you to believe blindly, but to build it with me.

examples.french: Notre ambition n'est pas de suivre le marché, mais de le devancer.
examples.english: Our ambition is not to follow the market, but to get ahead of it.

examples.french: Ce cap, nous le tiendrons ensemble, ou nous ne le tiendrons pas.
examples.english: We will hold this course together, or we will not hold it at all.

examples.french: Un discours mobilisateur se mesure à ce qu'il inspire, pas à ce qu'il promet.
examples.english: A rallying speech is measured by what it inspires, not by what it promises.

blocks.tip: Reserve superlatives for the closing line — a speech that opens at maximum intensity has nowhere left to climb.

blocks.heading: Les éléments de langage et la novlangue managériale
blocks.body: "Éléments de langage" (approved talking points) let a spokesperson stay on message across many audiences, but at C2 level a speaker must recognise when this discipline slides into "novlangue" — vague managerial jargon that empties language of meaning without saying anything falsifiable. Mastery means keeping the discipline while still saying something real.

examples.french: Nous restons alignés sur nos éléments de langage jusqu'à l'annonce officielle.
examples.english: We remain aligned on our talking points until the official announcement.

examples.french: « Optimiser les synergies » ne veut plus rien dire pour personne.
examples.english: "Optimising synergies" no longer means anything to anyone.

examples.french: Le jargon managérial rassure la direction et n'informe jamais le salarié.
examples.english: Management jargon reassures leadership and never informs the employee.

examples.french: Derrière la formule vague, il faut toujours chercher la décision réelle.
examples.english: Behind the vague phrase, one must always look for the real decision.

examples.french: Un bon communicant sait quand quitter les éléments de langage pour dire la vérité nue.
examples.english: A good communicator knows when to abandon the talking points and speak the plain truth.

blocks.tip: If a sentence would survive being read at any company, in any sector, on any subject, it is novlangue, not communication.

blocks.heading: Annoncer une mauvaise nouvelle : cadrer sans travestir
blocks.body: Corporate discourse is tested hardest when the news is bad — layoffs, missed targets, a failed launch. The C2 skill is framing (cadrer) reality without distorting (travestir) it: naming the difficulty plainly, taking responsibility in the "nous," and pairing the bad news with a credible next step rather than burying it in qualifiers.

examples.french: Nous n'avons pas atteint nos objectifs, et nous en assumons la responsabilité.
examples.english: We did not reach our targets, and we take responsibility for that.

examples.french: Cadrer une mauvaise nouvelle, ce n'est pas l'édulcorer, c'est la rendre audible.
examples.english: Framing bad news is not sweetening it, it's making it audible.

examples.french: Travestir un échec en succès finit toujours par se retourner contre son auteur.
examples.english: Dressing up a failure as a success always backfires on whoever does it.

examples.french: Voici ce que nous avons appris, et voici ce que nous changeons dès demain.
examples.english: Here is what we have learned, and here is what we are changing starting tomorrow.

examples.french: Le silence sur un échec se paie toujours plus cher que son aveu.
examples.english: Silence about a failure always costs more than admitting it.

blocks.tip: Put the hardest sentence first, not last — an audience that senses evasion stops listening to everything that follows.

items.example: Un enthousiasme mal calibré sonne aussi faux qu'un pessimisme excessif.

items.example: La novlangue managériale finit par vider les mots de leur sens.

items.example: Cadrer une mauvaise nouvelle demande plus de courage que de la taire.

items.example: Travestir un échec en succès finit toujours par se retourner contre son auteur.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel de prudence : dire sans affirmer
blocks.body: In corporate and press French, the conditional signals a claim the speaker will not personally certify — protecting the institution from liability while still communicating information. It appears constantly in results announcements, denials, and non-denials, and recognising it is essential to reading between the lines of any corporate statement.

examples.french: Les résultats du troisième trimestre seraient en deçà des prévisions.
examples.english: Third-quarter results are reportedly below forecasts.

examples.french: Un accord aurait été trouvé avec les syndicats en fin de soirée.
examples.english: An agreement was reportedly reached with the unions late in the evening.

examples.french: La direction n'aurait pas encore tranché sur le sort de l'usine.
examples.english: Management has apparently not yet decided the plant's fate.

examples.french: Nous ne confirmons ni n'infirmons les chiffres qui circuleraient.
examples.english: We neither confirm nor deny the figures said to be circulating.

examples.french: Employer le conditionnel, c'est parler sans s'engager formellement.
examples.english: Using the conditional is speaking without formally committing oneself.

blocks.tip: Whenever a company statement uses the conditional for a fact rather than a hypothesis, read it as 'this is true, but we won't be the ones who said so.'

blocks.heading: La nominalisation : du verbe à l'abstraction officielle
blocks.body: Corporate and institutional French favours turning a verb-driven statement into a noun phrase, distancing the actor and softening the action: "réorganiser" becomes "procéder à une réorganisation," "décider" becomes "prendre la décision de." This nominal style sounds more formal and less personally accountable — recognising it lets you translate it back into who did what.

examples.french: Nous procédons à une réorganisation du service commercial.
examples.english: We are carrying out a reorganisation of the sales department.

examples.french: La direction a pris la décision de suspendre le projet.
examples.english: Management has made the decision to suspend the project.

examples.french: Il a été procédé à une révision complète du budget.
examples.english: A full revision of the budget was carried out.

examples.french: La mise en œuvre du plan débutera au premier trimestre.
examples.english: Implementation of the plan will begin in the first quarter.

examples.french: L'annonce de la fermeture a suivi la publication des résultats.
examples.english: The announcement of the closure followed the publication of the results.

blocks.tip: Translate a nominalised corporate sentence back into 'who does what' — it is often the fastest way to see what is actually being said, or hidden.

passages.title: Une allocution qui tombe juste
passages.french:
Quand Élise Battier a pris la parole devant les huit cents salariés réunis dans l'auditorium, personne n'attendait un miracle.
Le groupe Vernoux venait d'annoncer la suppression de deux cents postes, et la novlangue habituelle aurait suffi à vider la salle de tout espoir.
Elle a choisi une autre voie. « Nous n'avons pas atteint nos objectifs, et nous en assumons la responsabilité », a-t-elle commencé, sans détour ni élément de langage superflu.
Plutôt que de travestir l'échec en simple ajustement stratégique, elle a nommé chaque erreur : un investissement lancé trop tôt, un marché mal évalué, des alertes internes ignorées trop longtemps.
Le silence dans la salle n'était plus celui de la méfiance, mais de l'attention.
« Ce trimestre a été difficile ; le prochain sera décisif », a-t-elle poursuivi, avant d'exposer, point par point, ce qui allait changer dès le mois suivant.
Aucune promesse chiffrée, aucun enthousiasme forcé — seulement une feuille de route précise et un aveu assumé.
Les analystes présents, habitués aux discours convenus, ont noté l'absence quasi totale de jargon managérial.
« Un bon communicant sait quand quitter les éléments de langage pour dire la vérité nue », a commenté un observateur en sortant.
Le lendemain, l'action du groupe n'avait pas bondi ; mais en interne, pour la première fois depuis des mois, la cohésion d'équipe semblait redevenue possible.
passages.english:
When Élise Battier took the floor in front of the eight hundred employees gathered in the auditorium, no one expected a miracle.
The Vernoux group had just announced the elimination of two hundred jobs, and the usual newspeak would have been enough to drain all hope from the room.
She chose another path. "We did not reach our targets, and we take responsibility for that," she began, with no detours or superfluous talking points.
Rather than dressing up the failure as a mere strategic adjustment, she named each mistake: an investment launched too early, a market misjudged, internal warnings ignored for too long.
The silence in the room was no longer one of distrust, but of attention.
"This quarter was difficult; the next will be decisive," she continued, before laying out, point by point, what was going to change starting the following month.
No figures promised, no forced enthusiasm — only a precise roadmap and an owned admission.
The analysts present, used to conventional speeches, noted the near-total absence of management jargon.
"A good communicator knows when to abandon the talking points and speak the plain truth," one observer remarked on the way out.
The next day, the group's share price had not surged; but internally, for the first time in months, team cohesion seemed possible again.

questions.answer: She names the concrete errors that led to the layoffs

questions.prompt: What effect does her directness have on the room?

questions.answer: The silence shifts from distrust to attention

lessons.title: La négociation complexe
lessons.description: Beyond diplomacy: read the balance of power, deploy anchoring and leverage, and close a high-stakes deal without ever showing your hand.

blocks.heading: Le rapport de force : lire la partie avant de la jouer
blocks.body: Before a single word is exchanged, every complex negotiation is shaped by an underlying rapport de force — who needs the deal more, who has alternatives, who controls the timeline. A C2-level negotiator reads this balance before opening their mouth, and never mistakes politeness for an absence of power dynamics.

examples.french: Le rapport de force a basculé dès que notre concurrent a annoncé son retrait.
examples.english: The balance of power shifted the moment our competitor announced its withdrawal.

examples.french: Celui qui a le moins besoin de l'accord détient, de fait, le plus de pouvoir.
examples.english: Whoever needs the deal least holds, in fact, the most power.

examples.french: Ne confondez jamais la courtoisie de votre interlocuteur avec une position de faiblesse.
examples.english: Never mistake your counterpart's courtesy for a position of weakness.

examples.french: Lire le rapport de force, c'est d'abord savoir qui peut se permettre d'attendre.
examples.english: Reading the balance of power starts with knowing who can afford to wait.

examples.french: Un bon négociateur évalue son propre levier avant même d'entrer dans la salle.
examples.english: A skilled negotiator assesses their own leverage before even entering the room.

blocks.tip: Ask yourself who walks away with less if the talks collapse today — that answer is the real starting position, whatever the opening speeches say.

blocks.heading: L'ancrage et la position de repli
blocks.body: Anchoring (l'ancrage) sets the reference point the rest of the negotiation will orbit around — the first credible figure spoken often shapes the final outcome disproportionately. Just as essential is knowing your own position de repli, the fallback you retreat to if the deal cannot be reached on better terms, and never revealing it before you must.

examples.french: Celui qui ancre le premier chiffre oriente toute la discussion qui suit.
examples.english: Whoever anchors the first figure shapes the entire discussion that follows.

examples.french: Ancrer trop haut sans justification décrédibilise l'ensemble de l'offre.
examples.english: Anchoring too high without justification undermines the whole offer's credibility.

examples.french: Définissez votre position de repli avant d'entrer dans la salle, jamais pendant.
examples.english: Define your fallback position before entering the room, never during.

examples.french: Révéler sa position de repli, c'est offrir gratuitement son point de rupture à l'adversaire.
examples.english: Revealing your fallback position hands your opponent your breaking point for free.

examples.french: Le point de rupture n'est jamais un chiffre fixe ; il dépend de ce que vous êtes prêt à perdre.
examples.english: The breaking point is never a fixed number; it depends on what you're prepared to lose.

blocks.tip: Write your walk-away number down before the meeting — under pressure, the mind quietly revises it upward without telling you.

blocks.heading: Les tactiques de pouvoir : lever, temporiser, déstabiliser
blocks.body: Complex negotiation deploys tactics well beyond diplomatic phrasing: exercer un levier to convert an advantage into concrete concessions, temporiser to buy time when a position is not yet ready, or déstabiliser a counterpart with a calculated silence or a sudden change of pace. None of these require raising one's voice — the most effective ones rarely do.

examples.french: Elle a su exercer un levier décisif au moment où l'accord semblait acquis.
examples.english: She managed to exert decisive leverage right when the deal seemed secured.

examples.french: Temporiser n'est pas hésiter : c'est attendre que le rapport de force évolue.
examples.english: Stalling is not hesitating: it's waiting for the balance of power to shift.

examples.french: Un silence bien placé déstabilise plus sûrement qu'une objection frontale.
examples.english: A well-placed silence unsettles more surely than a head-on objection.

examples.french: Elle a laissé traîner la réponse trois jours, sans jamais s'excuser du délai.
examples.english: She let the reply drag on for three days, never apologising for the delay.

examples.french: Reprendre la main après une concession exige un aplomb que peu maîtrisent.
examples.english: Regaining the upper hand after a concession requires a composure few master.

blocks.tip: A tactic used too often stops working — rotate leverage, stalling, and silence rather than leaning on a single move.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel passé : évoquer ce qui aurait pu être
blocks.body: In negotiation debriefs and in real-time bargaining alike, the past conditional (aurait + participle) lets a speaker evoke a counterfactual scenario — what could have been obtained, conceded, or avoided under different conditions — without directly reproaching anyone. Paired with 'si' + plus-que-parfait, it reframes a past failure as a lesson rather than an accusation.

examples.french: Si nous avions ancré plus haut, nous aurions sans doute obtenu davantage.
examples.english: Had we anchored higher, we would likely have gotten more.

examples.french: Vous auriez pu nous prévenir avant de changer les conditions.
examples.english: You could have warned us before changing the terms.

examples.french: Sans cette fuite d'information, l'accord aurait été signé dès mardi.
examples.english: Without that information leak, the deal would have been signed by Tuesday.

examples.french: Elle aurait accepté la première offre si le calendrier n'avait pas été aussi serré.
examples.english: She would have accepted the first offer had the timeline not been so tight.

examples.french: Ce round de négociation, mal préparé, n'aurait jamais dû commencer ainsi.
examples.english: This round of negotiation, poorly prepared, should never have started that way.

blocks.tip: The past conditional lets you name a mistake in the room without naming who made it — useful when the person who erred is still sitting across the table.

blocks.heading: À moins que, pour peu que : poser une condition avec doigté
blocks.body: 'À moins que' (unless, + subjunctive, often with an optional 'ne' explétif) and 'pour peu que' (if only, provided that, + subjunctive) let a negotiator state a condition or a veiled threat without sounding like an ultimatum — the subjunctive itself signals that the outcome is still hypothetical, leaving room to negotiate the condition too.

examples.french: Nous signerons cette semaine, à moins que le prix ne soit revu à la baisse.
examples.english: We will sign this week, unless the price is revised downward.

examples.french: Pour peu que vous acceptiez ce délai, l'accord est pratiquement conclu.
examples.english: Provided you accept this deadline, the deal is practically done.

examples.french: À moins qu'un accord ne soit trouvé d'ici vendredi, nous nous retirons de la table.
examples.english: Unless an agreement is reached by Friday, we are withdrawing from the table.

examples.french: Pour peu qu'une seule clause bouge, tout l'équilibre de l'accord s'effondre.
examples.english: If even a single clause moves, the whole balance of the deal collapses.

blocks.tip: The optional 'ne' after 'à moins que' (ne soit, ne bouge) is a mark of careful register — it changes nothing in meaning, but signals a controlled, formal voice.

passages.title: Le rachat qui a failli capoter
passages.french:
L'acquisition de Tellien Systèmes par le groupe Arka Capital devait être bouclée en six semaines ; elle en a pris quatre mois.
Dès la première séance, Arka Capital avait ancré son offre à un niveau volontairement bas, pariant sur l'urgence de trésorerie de Tellien.
Le rapport de force semblait clair — jusqu'à ce que Tellien annonce, sans prévenir, l'intérêt d'un second acquéreur.
« C'était du bluff pur, a reconnu plus tard un des négociateurs d'Arka, mais nous ne pouvions pas prendre le risque de vérifier. »
La marge de manœuvre d'Arka s'est aussitôt réduite, et son équipe a dû revoir sa position de repli en quelques heures.
Vint alors la phase la plus tendue : trois semaines de tactique dilatoire de part et d'autre, chacun attendant que l'autre bouge en premier.
« Pour peu qu'une seule clause bouge, tout l'équilibre de l'accord s'effondre », a résumé un conseiller juridique présent aux dernières séances.
Le point de blocage final ne portait ni sur le prix ni sur le calendrier, mais sur une clause de non-concurrence jugée trop large.
Arka a fini par lâcher du lest sur ce point précis, en échange d'une garantie sur les effectifs.
« Nous avons dû reprendre la main sans donner l'impression de céder », a expliqué la directrice des fusions-acquisitions d'Arka.
L'accord a finalement été signé un vendredi soir, sans communiqué de presse avant le lundi suivant — le temps, disaient certains, de laisser le rapport de force se stabiliser avant de l'annoncer au marché.
passages.english:
The acquisition of Tellien Systèmes by the Arka Capital group was meant to close in six weeks; it took four months.
From the first session, Arka Capital had anchored its offer at a deliberately low level, betting on Tellien's cash-flow urgency.
The balance of power seemed clear — until Tellien announced, without warning, the interest of a second buyer.
"It was pure bluff," one of Arka's negotiators later admitted, "but we couldn't risk checking."
Arka's room to manoeuvre shrank immediately, and its team had to revise its fallback position within hours.
Then came the tensest phase: three weeks of stalling tactics on both sides, each waiting for the other to move first.
"If even a single clause moves, the whole balance of the deal collapses," summarised a legal adviser present at the final sessions.
The final sticking point concerned neither the price nor the schedule, but a non-compete clause deemed too broad.
Arka eventually gave ground on that specific point, in exchange for a guarantee on staffing levels.
"We had to regain the upper hand without appearing to give in," explained Arka's head of mergers and acquisitions.
The deal was finally signed on a Friday evening, with no press release before the following Monday — time, some said, to let the balance of power settle before announcing it to the market.

lessons.title: Le conseil
lessons.description: The advisory register: recommend with authority, hedge with precision, and give a client counsel they can act on without ever overstating your certainty.

blocks.heading: Recommander sans dicter : l'autorité mesurée du conseil
blocks.body: Expert advice must sound authoritative without becoming an order — the consultant informs a decision the client still owns. C2-level advisory register balances confident verbs (préconiser, recommander) with hedges (à notre sens, sous réserve de) that mark the limits of what the advisor can guarantee, letting authority and honesty coexist in the same sentence.

examples.french: Nous préconisons une réorganisation progressive, plutôt qu'un big bang.
examples.english: We recommend a gradual reorganisation, rather than a big bang.

examples.french: À notre sens, le risque principal ne réside pas là où vous le situez.
examples.english: In our view, the main risk does not lie where you place it.

examples.french: Cette recommandation reste valable sous réserve d'une validation juridique.
examples.english: This recommendation remains valid subject to legal validation.

examples.french: Nous ne décidons pas à votre place ; nous éclairons la décision.
examples.english: We do not decide in your place; we inform the decision.

examples.french: Un conseil sans réserve affichée n'est jamais tout à fait honnête.
examples.english: Advice with no stated caveat is never entirely honest.

blocks.tip: State your recommendation before your hedge, not after — leading with the caveat makes even solid advice sound tentative.

blocks.heading: Le diagnostic avant la recommandation
blocks.body: No credible advisory register skips the diagnostic phase: before recommending anything, the consultant must objectiver the situation, name the working hypothesis, and show the client the reasoning, not only the conclusion. A recommendation without a visible diagnostic reads as an opinion; with one, it reads as expertise.

examples.french: Avant toute recommandation, il convient d'objectiver la situation actuelle.
examples.english: Before any recommendation, the current situation must be substantiated with evidence.

examples.french: Notre hypothèse de travail repose sur trois entretiens et l'analyse des chiffres transmis.
examples.english: Our working hypothesis rests on three interviews and the analysis of the figures provided.

examples.french: Le diagnostic précède toujours la préconisation, jamais l'inverse.
examples.english: The diagnosis always precedes the recommendation, never the reverse.

examples.french: Sans diagnostic partagé, aucun plan d'action ne tient dans la durée.
examples.english: Without a shared diagnosis, no action plan holds up over time.

examples.french: Nous avons cherché à étayer chaque constat par une donnée vérifiable.
examples.english: We sought to substantiate every finding with a verifiable data point.

blocks.tip: If a client cannot repeat your diagnostic in their own words, your recommendation will not survive their first internal meeting.

blocks.heading: La juste distance : l'accompagnement sans l'ingérence
blocks.body: The consultant's authority depends on staying close enough to understand the client's reality, yet distant enough to keep the outside perspective (le regard extérieur) that justified hiring them in the first place. Good accompagnement guides implementation without quietly taking over decisions that must remain the client's own.

examples.french: Notre rôle est d'accompagner la décision, pas de la prendre à votre place.
examples.english: Our role is to support the decision, not to make it in your place.

examples.french: Le regard extérieur perd toute sa valeur dès qu'il se laisse absorber par l'interne.
examples.english: The outside perspective loses all its value the moment it gets absorbed into the internal view.

examples.french: Nous restons disponibles pendant la mise en œuvre, sans nous y substituer.
examples.english: We remain available during implementation, without taking it over ourselves.

examples.french: Un bon consultant sait quand se retirer, pas seulement quand intervenir.
examples.english: A good consultant knows when to step back, not only when to step in.

examples.french: L'accompagnement s'arrête là où commence la dépendance du client.
examples.english: Support ends where the client's dependency begins.

blocks.tip: The moment a client can no longer make a decision without you, the advisory relationship has gone wrong — even if it feels indispensable.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel pour formuler une recommandation avec prudence
blocks.body: Advisory French uses the conditional to propose a course of action without imposing it: 'il conviendrait de,' 'il serait souhaitable de,' 'nous suggérerions.' This softens the directive force of a recommendation while keeping it unambiguous — the client hears a suggestion backed by expertise, not an order issued by an outsider.

examples.french: Il conviendrait de tester cette hypothèse avant de généraliser la solution.
examples.english: It would be advisable to test this hypothesis before generalising the solution.

examples.french: Nous suggérerions de reporter le déploiement de deux semaines.
examples.english: We would suggest postponing the rollout by two weeks.

examples.french: Il serait souhaitable de revoir ce calendrier dès la semaine prochaine.
examples.english: It would be desirable to revisit this schedule as early as next week.

examples.french: Une communication interne préalable serait, à notre sens, indispensable.
examples.english: Prior internal communication would, in our view, be essential.

examples.french: Nous ne saurions trop recommander une phase pilote avant le déploiement complet.
examples.english: We cannot recommend a pilot phase strongly enough before full rollout.

blocks.tip: 'Nous ne saurions trop recommander' is a fixed, elegant intensifier — it sounds modest in form while making the strongest possible recommendation.

blocks.heading: Le gérondif et les propositions participiales dans le rapport de conseil
blocks.body: Consulting reports lean on the gerund (en + present participle) and participial clauses to compress two related ideas into a single, efficient sentence — showing cause, manner, or simultaneity without a second full clause. This tightens the analytical, written register that separates a report from a spoken conversation.

examples.french: En objectivant la situation, l'équipe a évité plusieurs décisions hâtives.
examples.english: By substantiating the situation, the team avoided several hasty decisions.

examples.french: Le diagnostic, une fois partagé, a changé la nature même de la discussion.
examples.english: The diagnosis, once shared, changed the very nature of the discussion.

examples.french: Ayant audité l'ensemble du processus, le cabinet a pu chiffrer précisément les gains attendus.
examples.english: Having audited the entire process, the firm was able to precisely quantify the expected gains.

examples.french: En recommandant une approche progressive, nous limitons le risque d'exécution.
examples.english: By recommending a gradual approach, we limit execution risk.

examples.french: Le plan d'action, restant volontairement bref, tient sur une seule page.
examples.english: The action plan, deliberately kept brief, fits on a single page.

blocks.tip: Reach for a participial clause ('le diagnostic, une fois partagé...') whenever a second 'et' clause would slow the sentence down without adding real information.

passages.title: Le diagnostic qui dérangeait
passages.french:
Le cabinet Orsel & Vennec avait été mandaté par le groupe Ferrand Industries pour une mission de conseil de trois mois, officiellement centrée sur l'optimisation logistique.
Dès la deuxième semaine, la consultante en charge du dossier, Camille Reig, a émis des réserves sur le périmètre même de la mission.
« Avant toute recommandation, il convient d'objectiver la situation actuelle », a-t-elle rappelé au comité de direction, avant de présenter un premier constat qui ne portait pas sur la logistique, mais sur la gouvernance interne.
La direction, surprise, a d'abord contesté la méthode.
« Notre hypothèse de travail repose sur trois entretiens et l'analyse des chiffres transmis, pas sur une opinion », a répondu Camille, sans se départir de son calme.
Le diagnostic, une fois partagé avec l'ensemble du comité, a changé la nature même de la mission.
« À notre sens, le risque principal ne réside pas là où vous le situez », a-t-elle préconisé, avant d'ajouter une réserve importante : la recommandation restait valable sous réserve d'un accès complet aux données financières, encore partiellement refusé.
Le cabinet a alors proposé un plan d'action en deux phases, la première consacrée à la gouvernance, la seconde seulement à la logistique initialement prévue.
« Nous ne décidons pas à votre place ; nous éclairons la décision », a rappelé Camille lors de la restitution finale.
La direction a fini par accepter le plan révisé, non sans réticence.
Trois mois plus tard, le livrable initial — un audit logistique — avait cédé la place à une feuille de route de gouvernance entièrement nouvelle, preuve, selon Camille, qu'un bon diagnostic dérange parfois davantage qu'il ne rassure.
passages.english:
The Orsel & Vennec firm had been hired by the Ferrand Industries group for a three-month consulting engagement, officially focused on logistics optimisation.
By the second week, the consultant in charge of the file, Camille Reig, had raised reservations about the very scope of the engagement.
"Before any recommendation, the current situation must be substantiated with evidence," she reminded the leadership committee, before presenting an initial finding that concerned not logistics, but internal governance.
Leadership, surprised, first challenged the method.
"Our working hypothesis rests on three interviews and the analysis of the figures provided, not on an opinion," Camille replied, without losing her composure.
The diagnosis, once shared with the whole committee, changed the very nature of the engagement.
"In our view, the main risk does not lie where you place it," she advised, before adding an important caveat: the recommendation remained valid subject to full access to the financial data, which was still partly withheld.
The firm then proposed a two-phase action plan, the first devoted to governance, the second only to the logistics work originally planned.
"We do not decide in your place; we inform the decision," Camille reminded them during the final debrief.
Leadership eventually accepted the revised plan, not without reluctance.
Three months later, the original deliverable — a logistics audit — had given way to an entirely new governance roadmap, proof, according to Camille, that a good diagnosis sometimes unsettles more than it reassures.
